sections.heading: Supporting analysis: product scoping for the DS + AI offering
sections.text: *20 Oct 2026.* Labels: O observed · D documented, unverified · I inferred · U unknown. Every number here is in evidence-index.md. Paths are relative to DS Pratice/demo tools/ unless stated.

sections.heading: 1.1 The three projects at a glance
sections.text:
DSN (Rui) · DS Starter Pack + Configurator (Nuno) · ASSA prototyping kit v5 (Raquel, client work)

What it is · Nagarro's own AI-first React component library, plus a docs site with editors, MCP and a CLI · A GitHub template for a client-owned DS on Base UI, plus a configurator app with a wizard, a Claude agent and a Figma plugin · A prototyping tool on the client's real design system: designers type start, Claude builds on-system screens
Production or prototype? · Closest to production: ds-ngr 0.1.44, ~1,123 tests, 8 CI workflows, an npm publish workflow (O) · Template, private: true, not installable yet (O) · Prototype only: "not meant to ship to production" (README.md:9-11, O)
Components · 104 public (O) · 56 specs, 48 story files (O) · 43 component folders, 61 custom elements (O)
Implementation · React + plain CSS, .dsn-* classes (O) · React 19 + Base UI wrappers (O) · Framework-free custom elements, light DOM (O)
Tokens · 431 DTCG tokens; 3 layers, 8 semantic tiers; single brand + light/dark (O) · 190 semantic variables → 522 CSS properties; brands gold/violet; density as a multiplier (O) · 414 Figma variables in Brand/Theme/Device/_Core, all with code names; 2 brands × 2 themes × 3 devices (O)
Source of truth · Mixed: primitives from Figma, semantic tokens hand-kept in tokens.css, themes on the site (O) · Split: tokens from Figma, components from specs, theme from the configurator (O) · Figma first, then core/, then prototypes (O)
Design↔code alignment · 7 audit scripts + 2 weekly cron checks; sync-components reports 97 drift items (O, run 20 Oct) · Parity script (local, not in CI); plugin 3-way review (O) · binding-parity fails the build on mismatch; ±1px fidelity check; checks run in hooks after every edit (O)
AI layer · ds-index.json, 46 "absences" (names that don't exist), closed vocabulary.json, 23-tool MCP, 8 skills, llms.txt (O) · llms.txt, one skill, theme and prototype agents limited to a schema, Undo/Keep review (O) · One governance skill enforced by hooks; machine-readable meta.json per component (O)
Editing UI · Site: customize a component → opens a GitHub PR; spec, AI-rules and skill editors. Repo writes only in local dev; editor AI assist is mocked (O) · Configurator edits theme intents and component-token overrides; writes one file, ds.project.json; no PR (O) · No GUI; changes go through Claude chat; "propose → confirm → apply" for Figma (O)
Brownfield · None. Closest: a self-audit checklist and the ds-patrol skill (O) · "Mirror an existing Figma system" is Coming later (seen in the running app, O); import only fits files derived from the starter (I) · The only real brownfield case: an existing client kit, restructured by hand (O for the result; the "211 → 414" before figure is U in this copy)
Reusable vs specific · Pattern reusable; content is Nagarro-branded (O) · Generic; no client leak in the repo (O). The shared Figma file has an assa_abloy_test mode (prior session, O) · Engine reusable after de-branding; Figma keys, fonts, brand and portal content are Client IP (O)

The configurator video (nuno_ds_configurator.mov, 4 min 05 s, 17 sampled frames, O):
- live theming on a bento of real components;
- the Variables table;
- a Button override editor showing "applies to N bindings";
- export to the "Variable Test" Figma file, where the plugin applied 252 changes with 1 failure ("font/family/primary … unloaded font", at ~3:15).

It is a credible demo of Path A, and it is honest about edge cases.

sections.heading: 1.2 How they relate
sections.text:
```
Path A (start new)                         Path B (bring your system)
Starter Pack template ── wizard ── theme ──┐       nothing today ── (ASSA: done by hand as a service)
                                           ▼
                     Figma plugin 3-way review  ◄──── shared idea: change sets reviewed in Figma
DSN AI layer (index, absences, MCP, skills) ──► could serve any system that has a contract
DSN site editors (customize → PR) ─────────────► closest thing to the "editable Storybook"
ASSA gates (binding parity, Figma-first, hooks) ► the strictest governance pattern
```

Duplicates to resolve:
- 2 theme configurators: DSN /brands and the Starter Pack editor.
- 3 "prototype a screen" features: DSN prototype canvas, the Starter Pack prototype agent, the ASSA kit.
- 2 greenfield starters: DSN create makes a client app on DSN; the Starter Pack makes a client-owned design system.

Conflicts:
- 3 token grammars. DSN tokens.css holds both the accent-strong and interactive-primary families (O, grep), so the board's mismatch tile is a simplification.
- DSN vocabulary.json maps pressed → active, while the Starter Pack ships -pressed tokens (O).
- Stale docs everywhere:
  - DSN README says Styled Components, the code is plain CSS.
  - Starter Pack llms.txt says 49 components, there are 56 specs.
  - ASSA README links to a maintainers/ folder that the zip excludes.

sections.heading: 2.1 Goals and problems (as written on the board)
sections.text:
- North star: "The internal center of excellence for Design Systems — and the leading voice on AI-ready design at scale."
- Success: internal teams regularly engage the practice; new business through the practice; clients request the offering; recognized as the reference group.
- Problems (*Where are we today?*):
  - demos and deliveries first, design ops after;
  - everyone builds a DS from scratch, their own way;
  - DS proposal slides rebuilt every time;
  - no decision map for client scenarios;
  - designers outside Portugal lack knowledge;
  - no updated onboarding file.
- Priorities: Offers & Proposals ("evaluate the whole narrative as one") · Education · Awareness · Demos (DS Accelerator, DS Configurator).
- Business opportunities: AI-ready DS · multi-brand / enterprise · personalized CLI (?) · "AI prototypes → you will need a design system".
- Gaps (WIP): "Selling time-to-market faster". Listed competition: Accenture Song, Deloitte, Capgemini, EPAM, Southleft.
- DS Accelerator notes (354:2661), exploratory, not decided:
  - "Flow: you put the source of the Figma link, Jira ticket or code repository → it analyses → proposes solutions for code"
  - "Foundation for all / Accelerate existing things / Internal + Clients"
  - "Inspiration: similar to the Claude Artifacts/Design experience"
  - "clients don't empathize seeing code on VSCode"

sections.heading: 2.2 How we describe and demo the offering today
sections.text:
- Packages (decided 19 Oct): 2-week AI audit · DS Build · DS Accelerate · DS Scale · Support.
- Assets: the registry in 331:914 lists 5 tools, 9 demos, 7 templates, 8 decks, 11 docs and 8 content items.
- What to use when: 335:640 routes 5 situations + 13 axes to assets. It already exposes the gaps: no native starter, no Tailwind/MUI adapter, no migration playbook, no Tokens Studio import.
- Earlier vision (297:285): "one engine, four modules (Assess, Configure, Build/prototype, Hand off), three views (workbench, client share link, public showcase)", 9 lo-fi screens.

sections.text:

Recommendation sides with in-repo for the client tool and keeps a thin Nagarro view only for demos
What the client keeps · Decided: "deliverable is the client-owned system, not the tool" · n/a · "the client would retain a tool for managing the system" · Tension, resolvable: the panel ships in the client repo, so it is part of the owned system
Plug-and-play · Decision map shows many stacks we can't serve · React only (O) · "not plug-and-play; many tools already offer that" · Agree: be explicit about the supported profile
One Nagarro DS · D8 public showcase option · 3 libraries, 3 grammars (O) · not discussed · Open (D2/D8): not required for this product
Already implemented · Configurator, plugin, MCP, skills, starter, audits · (O) · Reuse
Missing · Assess module, convergence/migration, govern dashboard · No brownfield import, no PR from the configurator, no hosted backend (O) · "adaptation phase for an existing system" · Build thin, behind a test

What changed my recommendation because of the board:
- The Audit's *selling* problems (proposal slides rebuilt, no decision map, demos before design ops) mean the product must first make a repeatable demo and assessment, not a feature-rich editor.
- The decision map's honest gaps mean we must name a supported profile instead of claiming universality.
- The 297:285 workbench idea is kept only as the *Nagarro-side* demo/assessment view.

sections.heading: 3. Users, buyers and jobs
sections.text:
Who · Role · Job to be done

Seller (account lead, presales, practice member) · Internal user · "When a prospect says their system is messy or AI output is generic, I want to show in 10 minutes what we'd find, fix and leave behind, so I can book the 2-week audit."
Delivery designer/engineer on a client project · Internal user · "When an engagement starts, I want a repeatable start (template or assessment), so I don't rebuild a design system my own way."
Client DS maintainer (design + engineering) · Client user, daily · "When I change a token or a component's guidance, I want to see the impact and get it reviewed in Figma and code, so the system doesn't drift."
Client product teams + their AI agents · Client user, consumer · "When I or an agent build UI, I want only real components and tokens used."
Buyer: Head of Design / DesignOps, Head of Front-end, CPO/CTO · Client decision-maker · "I want proof the investment keeps paying after the agency leaves." (ASSA deck slide 14: "It works for one product. Will it work for ten?")
Practice team (Raquel, Rui, Nuno) · Maintainers · "I want one thing to maintain, not three demos that drift."

Where the projects meet these jobs:
- Same journey: Starter Pack + DSN (start → theme → build → AI-assisted UI).
- Complementary: ASSA governance gates + the Starter Pack Figma review + DSN audits all serve "keep it from drifting".
- Conflicting purposes: DSN create gives a client an app on *Nagarro's* system; the Starter Pack gives the client *their own* system. Only the second matches the decided commercial model. DSN create stays for demos and prototypes.

sections.heading: 4. Options compared
sections.text:
Scoring: 1 (poor) to 5 (strong); it is a judgment, not measurement. Weights reflect the commercial objective (differentiation and user value count most) and our capacity (~1 day/week each, so maintenance and migration count double).

Criterion (weight) · 1 · Keep separate, clearer positioning · 2 · Share foundations, distinct tools · 3 · One experience, separate modules · 4 · One product + one codebase

User value (3) · 2 · 3 · 5 · 4
Differentiation (3) · 2 · 3 · 5 · 3
Supports demos and sales (2) · 3 · 3 · 5 · 4
What the client keeps (2) · 2 · 3 · 5 · 3
Adoption effort (1) · 5 · 4 · 3 · 1
Technical compatibility (2) · 5 · 4 · 3 · 2
Governance clarity (1) · 2 · 4 · 4 · 3
Maintenance cost (2) · 3 · 4 · 3 · 2
Migration risk (2) · 5 · 4 · 4 · 1
Keeps useful capabilities (1) · 5 · 5 · 4 · 2
Weighted average · 3.2 · 3.5 · 4.3 · 2.7

What each option means for service, demos, sales and what the client keeps:
1. Keep separate.
   - Cheapest, and already half done by zone 3 "What to use when".
   - Sellers still demo three tools and explain the gaps.
   - The client keeps a repo but no management layer.
   - Fails the team's differentiation goal.
2. Share foundations. A common system contract + shared checks.
   - Low risk, and it is the necessary first step anyway.
   - On its own the client experience is still fragmented.
3. One experience, separate modules. Recommended, reached through 2.
   - The client and the seller see one panel. The modules stay in their own codebases and owners.
   - Cost: a contract and adapters must exist before the panel is useful on a client system.
4. One codebase.
   - Means choosing one component implementation and one grammar.
   - Breaks Figma bindings in at least two files, the Code Connect mappings (44 + 90 files) and the configurator export mapping.
   - Delivers no client value that option 3 doesn't.

Merging the experience ≠ merging repositories, libraries or token systems. Option 3 merges what people *see and do*. Libraries and grammars stay separate. The contract + adapters translate between them.

Evidence that would change this:
- If Stage 0 shows our own three systems can't share one contract without per-system code → fall back to 2 (shared checks only) and keep Path B as a service with scripts.
- If clients in demo tests don't value the retained panel → 1 with better positioning is enough.
- If one client wants Nagarro's DS itself as their base (DSN create) → revisit D8 and option 4 for that line only.

sections.heading: 5. Tensions, and the position taken
sections.text:
Tension · Position

Duplicate repo + Figma vs adapt an existing system · Both are entry paths into the same panel. Duplicating is product (it exists). Adapting is service-first with a thin tool until the experiment passes.
In-repo layer vs separate app that imports · In-repo for the client tool: a dev server reading files from disk, the way Storybook reads stories and DSN's site imports ../src (O). A separate Nagarro-side view is fine for assessments and demos, and it only reads.
Different components, token models, brand structures · Don't converge the libraries. A small system contract describes any system (tokens in DTCG + role map, component metadata, rules/absences, Figma link). Adapters fill it. Modes vs tiers are both expressible (Carbon combines tiers + themes).
Figma-led vs spec-led truth · Per client, decided in the assessment and written into the contract (source: figma · spec · code per layer). Default to Raquel's practice rule: Figma leads tokens and component APIs. The Starter Pack's spec-led components are allowed when declared.
Existing drift · The scan reports it, people decide it: "fix in Figma" or "fix in code" per item (like the DSN ds-token-sync skill and the ASSA "fix the wrong side"). The tool never auto-resolves.
Guided edits, suggestions, review, approval · Suggestions come from rules we can show (DSN audits, the vocabulary, the ASSA lint), not free-form AI. Every edit is a branch + PR with checks. Approval is the client's existing PR review + CODEOWNERS (as in Primer / Changesets practice). Figma changes get the plugin's 3-way review.
Local, offline, hosted · MVP is local dev (both existing apps already are, O) + a static read-only share build for demos (the Starter Pack has docs:build with VITE_DS_READONLY, O). Hosted multi-user editing is excluded (keys, auth, storage are undecided: DSN store.ts "Hosting isn't chosen yet", O).
Prototype fidelity vs production · The panel manages the production system. Prototyping (ASSA kit, DSN canvas, Starter Pack prototype agent) is a consumer of it, kept separate. Never demo the ASSA prototypes as a library.
Repeatable tooling vs bespoke consulting · Standard: contract, panel, checks, the Figma plugin, the React adapter, the AI files. Bespoke: grammar mapping, drift decisions, missing metadata, governance setup, non-React stacks (see §7).
Sales demo vs ongoing client use · The demo needs inspect, suggest, impact and share link. Ongoing use needs PR, checks and Figma review. The MVP builds the demo path first on our own systems, then hardens what the pilot client uses.

sections.heading: 6.1 Proposition (one paragraph)
sections.text: Nagarro assesses and organizes your design system so design, code and AI agents use the same rules. You keep a control panel inside your own repository: it shows your real components, tokens and guidance, suggests improvements based on rules you can see, and turns every change into a reviewed pull request and a Figma change set. Checks in your pipeline stop drift and stop AI from inventing tokens. We bring the method, the tooling and a team for the hard parts. You keep the system and the means to run it.

sections.heading: 6.2 Users and outcomes
6.3 Main journeys
sections.text:
1. Start new (Path A, DS Build): "Use this template" → duplicate Figma → wizard (name, brands, modes, look) → panel opens on the same repo → add own components → handover.
2. Bring your system (Path B, 2-week AI audit → DS Accelerate / Scale): connect repo + Figma file (read-only) → assessment scan → readout (service) → adaptation (service: contract, grammar map, metadata) → panel live with checks → first changes as PRs → handover with a named owner.
3. Everyday change (client, after handover): open a component → see a suggestion → propose an edit → see the impact → PR + Figma review → merge.
4. Sell (internal): run the 8-step demo on a demo brand → leave a read-only share link → book the audit.

sections.heading: 6.4 Information architecture (the control panel)
sections.text:
- Overview: system health (checks passing, drift count, coverage), what changed recently.
- Components: the real component, variants, its tokens, its guidance (when to use, when not), its Figma link, its checks.
- Tokens: layers, modes and brands; where each token is used; Figma variable ↔ code name.
- Guidance & AI: rules, absences, skills, llms.txt/MCP status: what agents can read.
- Changes: proposals, open PRs, the Figma change sets waiting for review.
- Setup (Path A wizard / Path B adapter status).
- Share: read-only build for stakeholders.

sections.heading: 6.6 MVP, later, excluded
6.7 Conceptual architecture
sections.text:
```
Client repository (client owns)
├── design system code, tokens, docs, skills   ← real assets, unchanged formats
├── ds.contract.json  (v0)                     ← what the system is, where things live, source of truth per layer
├── control panel (dev dependency)             ← reads assets via adapters, writes edits to a branch
│     ├── adapters: tokens (DTCG / Figma export / CSS) · components (React, Storybook manifest if present) · docs/metadata
│     ├── rules: audits + vocabulary + absences    (from DSN, ASSA)
│     └── outputs: branch + PR · Figma change set · read-only share build
├── CI checks: parity, a11y, token audits, index up to date   (from all three)
└── AI files: llms.txt, MCP config, AGENTS.md, skills       (from DSN)
Figma file (client owns) ◄── plugin 3-way review ── change set   (from Starter Pack)
Nagarro (we own): assessment scan + playbook, adapter library, panel source, demo brand
```
Added 20 Oct, after the market research (market-trends.md):
- Channel publisher. The contract generates each agent format: Figma Specs / Make guidelines, Storybook MCP manifest, Claude Design import, v0/shadcn registry, DESIGN.md, AGENTS.md / skills / llms.txt.
- Evals. AI-generated UI is scored against the contract per release, across tools and models (Spotify Encore precedent), next to the CI checks.

Ownership: Nagarro owns the panel's source and the adapters (versioned, installed per client). The client owns everything in their repo and Figma file, including the installed panel version.

Sources of truth: declared per layer in the contract.

Module owners (proposal):
- the panel: one owner, Rui or Nuno (decision 5);
- the Figma bridge and Path A: Nuno;
- the AI layer: Rui;
- governance gates and the assessment method: Raquel.

Where adapters are unavoidable:
- token sources that aren't DTCG;
- grammar → role mapping;
- component discovery beyond React;
- Figma variable collections whose names don't match the code;
- missing component metadata (drafted from existing docs, completed by people).

Storybook 10's component manifest (React, preview) is a cheaper discovery source than parsing code ourselves, when a client already has Storybook.

sections.heading: 6.8 Service vs tool
sections.text:
Activity · Service · Tool

Assessment scan · interpret, prioritize, readout · runs checks, lists findings
Grammar and source-of-truth decisions · ✓ · records them in the contract
Adapter setup · fix mappings that don't fit · standard adapters
Drift resolution · decide per item · lists items, makes PRs
Component metadata · write and review · drafts from existing docs, validates
Governance owner, contribution model · ✓ · CODEOWNERS / PR template
Day-to-day changes · ✓ client-run
Support plan · periodic review · trends of checks

sections.heading: 7. What can be standardized vs what stays client-specific
sections.text:
Standard (product) · Client-specific (service)

Contract schema, panel, React adapter, Figma plugin, CI check set, AI files templates, assessment checks, demo brand · Token grammar mapping, source-of-truth per layer, drift decisions, component metadata content, brands, governance model, non-React stacks, migration of existing screens

sections.heading: 8. Demonstration journey
sections.text:
About 10 minutes, on the fictional demo brand (registry: *To do, 4 Nov*). Never on client IP externally.

# · Client problem · What you show · Outcome to say · Today?

1 · "We don't know how bad our system is" · Assessment scan of a messy demo system: drift, missing code names, contrast, what AI can't read · "A baseline in days, not opinions" · Proposed. Pieces exist as scripts (DSN audits, Starter Pack parity and contrast).
2 · "Has anyone fixed this before?" · ASSA before/after: four button sets became one Button (plus a separate IconButton); 414 of 414 values now have code names · "We did it for a global brand" · Exists, internal only until clearance. The 414 is verified; the before figures come from the Showcase deck v7 and are unverified in this copy.
3 · "Our designers and devs see different things" · Panel on the repo: the real Button, its tokens, guidance, Figma link · "One view of the real system" · Partly exists (DSN site component pages, Starter Pack docs site)
4 · "We don't know what good looks like" · A suggestion with its rule, e.g. "hover token equals default in dark mode" · "Best practice you can see, not a black box" · Rule exists (DSN audit-token-collisions); in-panel suggestion proposed
5 · "Changes break things we don't see" · Propose an edit, then the impact list (components, Figma bindings, docs) · "Know the blast radius before you merge" · Partly exists (Starter Pack override table shows "applies to N bindings"); impact on docs/Figma proposed
6 · "Figma and code drift apart" · PR with checks + the Figma plugin's 3-way review · "Reviewed in both tools" · Exists separately (DSN customize → PR in local dev; plugin review); joined proposed
7 · "AI makes things up" · An agent builds a screen from the real components; an invented token is refused · "AI stays on your system" · Exists (DSN MCP + absences; Starter Pack prototype agent)
8 · "What happens when you leave?" · Handover checklist: repo, Figma library, panel, checks, AI files, owner · "You own it and can run it" · Proposed

Greenfield variant: replace steps 1–2 with the wizard: "describe the look", the agent styles it, Undo/Keep, export to Figma. This exists (video, running app).
